stories.title: Mind2Act World benchmark tests robots on reasoning, action, and their combination
stories.summary: A new benchmark, Mind2Act World, evaluates embodied AI on cognitive reasoning, physical execution, and composing the two together in robotic manipulation tasks that most existing benchmarks test only separately.
stories.more: Mind2Act World is a new diagnostic benchmark for embodied AI that tests three capabilities together: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise physical execution, and the ability to compose the two through environmental feedback. The authors say most existing benchmarks evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks, or test them separately, but rarely check whether a system can combine them. That gap, they argue, makes it hard to tell whether a robot fails at manipulation tasks because of faulty reasoning, poor execution, or an inability to adapt one based on the other. The released excerpt does not name specific models or robot platforms evaluated against the new benchmark.

stories.title: Coda-DaVinci studies how code-based proxies shape AI video generation quality
stories.summary: A new study, Coda-DaVinci, examines how the 3D code proxies used in Code2Video should be built for the best video generation quality, finding task-dependent trade-offs between proxy granularity and realism.
stories.more: Code2Video is an existing approach that uses agent-authored 3D proxies to steer video generation, giving explicit control over structure and dynamics. Coda-DaVinci studies how those proxies and prompts should be constructed for the best downstream video quality, an area the authors say was underexplored. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, the researchers tested proxy granularity and physics simulation choices. They found the results depend on the task: coarser proxies produced more natural motion, while the excerpt is cut off before detailing the effects of medium and fine-grained proxies.

stories.title: HiUni extends a vision-language model to unify visual understanding and generation
stories.summary: HiUni is a new unified multimodal model that explores extending a pretrained vision-language model directly into one system for both visual understanding and generation, rather than keeping them separate.
stories.more: Unified multimodal models try to support both visual understanding and generation within a single framework, but prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to meet each task's different requirements. HiUni revisits that design choice, exploring whether a pretrained vision-language model can be directly extended into a unified model instead. The excerpt describing the approach is cut off before detailing parameter scale or specific results achieved.

stories.title: EgoCaptioner aims for more detailed, precisely timed egocentric video captions
stories.summary: EgoCaptioner is a new approach to egocentric video captioning that pairs a scene-level overview with precisely timed, detail-adaptive narration, addressing timing and detail gaps in current multimodal models.
stories.more: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, but current multimodal large language models often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misread the wearer's motion, the authors say. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. EgoCaptioner addresses this by pairing a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying levels of detail. The excerpt does not specify what models or datasets were used to evaluate EgoCaptioner.

stories.title: Anthropic completes largest-ever IPO, valued near $1.5 trillion
stories.summary: Anthropic went public in what's described as the largest IPO in history: shares (ANT) priced at $83, opened at $111.50, and closed at $97.17, valuing the company near $1.5 trillion.
stories.more: Anthropic's stock, trading under the ticker ANT, priced at $83 ahead of its public debut on November 19, 2026. Shares opened at $111.50 and closed the day at $97.17, valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion. The listing is described as the largest IPO in history. The same roundup separately notes that Google has opened its Genie 4 model to developers, though no further detail on that is given in this excerpt.

stories.title: 16-year-old founder launches Polemos, an AI missile startup chasing 'cost per kill'
stories.summary: Henrijs Dandzbergs, 16, dropped out of high school for Y Combinator to found Polemos, developing a new breed of AI-guided missile meant to lower the 'cost per kill' for the US and its allies.
stories.more: Henrijs Dandzbergs dropped out of high school to join Y Combinator, the startup accelerator, and founded Polemos. The company is developing what it describes as a new breed of missile intended to make killing as efficient as possible for the US and its military allies. The stated focus is on reducing 'cost per kill,' a metric framing munitions effectiveness in economic terms. The excerpt does not specify the missile's technical design, funding raised, or current development stage.

stories.title: WeMM-Video launches as open bilingual omni-modal video model family
stories.summary: WeMM-Video is a new family of open Chinese-English omni-modal foundation models, from 2B to 35B parameters, built for joint audio-visual video understanding and reasoning.
stories.more: WeMM-Video is a new family of bilingual Chinese-English omni-modal foundation models, released in 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B parameter sizes. It centers on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, unifying text, image, audio, and video processing in a hybrid-thinking paradigm. The models support a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses, with the paper framing the work as advancing open-source omni-modal video understanding. The excerpt available does not include benchmark comparisons against other video-understanding models.

stories.title: Nous Research brings open-source Hermes Agent's 'Collective Wisdom' to MS Teams
stories.summary: Nous Research's open-source Hermes Agent is coming to Microsoft Teams, with a new Collective Wisdom feature that turns one employee's AI workflow trick into a skill the whole team can use.
stories.more: Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent from Nous Research that companies will soon be able to run directly inside Microsoft Teams. Its new Collective Wisdom feature is designed to take an AI technique or shortcut discovered by one employee and turn it into a skill usable by the rest of the team. The excerpt does not specify a release date, pricing, or which Teams plans will support the integration.
